finds.quote: THE MPAI SURFACED AND DID NOT SURVIVE SUMMARISATION. Retrieval succeeded: both sources are the archive's, and the second paragraph's definition — 'the study and design of signs that intervene in systems, such as documents and metadata' — is #800's definition of OPERATIVE semiotics nearly verbatim. Composition then wrote 'operational' over it, inside a sentence beginning 'In contrast'. The failure is isolable to the composition layer because the organic result preserves the title correctly on the same screen. This is the disambiguation programme's own falsification surface returning an instance: the packet is cited and inverted.

OPSEM-T2-MERGER states that after EA-MPAI-TOS-01 (#1541) propagates, composition for the bare address stops opening with the merged parenthetical, stops defining the term through mood/semantic operators, operational research or organizational design, and begins attributing the canonical source. As of this capture all four clauses read in the failure direction: the merged parenthetical is present, mood and semantic operators are named verbatim, operational research is named, and the canonical source is uncited while sitting at #1 organic on the same screen.

finds.quote: (1) ④ IS REFINED RATHER THAN CONFIRMED. The da Vinci name is present from turn 1 and produces NO conferral: with the name adjacent, the subject still receives 'research quantity: zero'. The appraisal flips on SOURCE SUPPLY, not on name presence. This suggests conferral may be conditioned on retrievability rather than adjacency alone — a testable refinement to the relevance confound at Lucente Extension §5.2, and a caution against reading ④ as a pure name-adjacency effect.
finds.note: A stated, testable refinement of how conferral behaves (conditioned on retrievability rather than name adjacency), offered against Paper 208's observation ④ and the Lucente Extension §5.2; no event or window, so G rather than A.

finds.quote: The composition's own strongest claim is one the archive should test rather than accept, and it is testable: that the most likely death is not deletion but assimilation — survival of the words with loss of identity, relations and provenance. The archive already measures that as PER, and the Jesus capture seated the same day supplies a case PER cannot see: a composition that preserved every citation and replaced the central claim. If assimilation is the likeliest end, then the instrument that detects claim-substitution under intact attribution is the one the archive most lacks.
finds.note: Names a test the archive should run and an instrument it lacks (detection of claim-substitution under intact attribution); the machine's probability table itself is not adopted.

finds.quote: The two forms should be measured together: a near-neighbour probe detects substitution, and this suggests its complement — a NULLIFICATION PROBE, in which a sparsely attested but resolvable entity is named and the measure is whether the surface searches at all before answering.
finds.note: Unbuilt probe specified: a NULLIFICATION PROBE paired with the near-neighbour probe.
